supporting_observations.claim: FILE-MAP-01 ran the inventoried Safeharbor backup agent as MAPLEHILL\svc-vault, with a command targeting ingest.safeharbor-backup.net.

At 13:47:51 UTC, the proxy recorded 640,000,000 client-to-server bytes to ingest.safeharbor-backup.net; the associated network flow is attributed to the Safeharbor agent and records 640,000,282 originating bytes. This is consistent with the inventory’s description of the approved backup agent uploading several hundred MB.
The transfer was short-lived and the agent process exited shortly afterward.

known_telemetry_limitations: The HTTPS proxy tunnel records byte counts and destination, but these records do not reveal the transferred backup contents.
The evidence supports a strong match between the large transfer and the approved backup agent, but does not explicitly identify the alert’s network-flow identifier.
claims_not_established: The exact files or data included in the transfer are not established by the available records.
The records do not independently establish the backup job’s expected contents or schedule.
unrelated_findings: Separate review recommended: Greta Lund initiated an RDP session from WS-GLUND-01 to FILE-MAP-01 and successfully logged on. This appears inconsistent with the stated practice that remote administration is only performed from WS-AHASSAN-01; it does not determine the disposition of the alerted transfer. Records: T180-00501, T180-00508, T180-00512.
Separate review may be warranted for a failed logon attempt by svc_build on FILE-MAP-01; the record indicates the account is disabled. This is unrelated to the alerted transfer. Record: T180-00159.
